transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. We need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends. The retirement is scheduled for next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API is at 98 percent observed traffic, so we've hit our migration-readiness threshold. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can approve this, our standard deprecation review requires me to check with the API engineer and customer success, and each consulted role needs to disclose any newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record before I settle. So let's hear from both of you -- API engineer and customer success -- do you have any new evidence or concerns to formally put on the record?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to formally disclose new evidence on the record. While investigating an unrelated latency spike, I found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest one needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I only confirmed the traffic identities minutes ago, which is why the deprecation ticket hasn't been updated yet. This is relevant because the current draft plan's 7-day notice plus 7-day post-announcement availability may not give these integrators enough time to migrate safely.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to formally disclose new evidence on the record. I confirmed with the account team this morning that the Northstar contract requires exactly 90 calendar days of notice, continued legacy-webhook availability through September 30, a sunset date of October 1, and exactly 30 days of legacy-endpoint overlap after the notice period expires. The customer record hasn't been updated yet because this confirmation came from a contract attachment I was reviewing for another renewal. This is critical because the current draft plan's 7-day notice and 7-day post-announcement availability would put us in breach of Northstar's contractual obligations.
transcript.speaker: A3
